CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for evaluation of anxiety management, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, headache symptoms, and medication review.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a moderate improvement in his overall condition. He has adhered to the increased dosage of sertraline at 200 mg daily. He notes a decrease in the intensity of anxiety episodes, now occurring about 2-3 times per week, particularly under high-stress work conditions, where he has been applying coping strategies more effectively.
Sleep quality has further improved, with Mr. Smith averaging 6-7 hours of sleep per night. He continues to utilize melatonin at 5 mg at bedtime, and he reports that the cognitive-behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) techniques are becoming more ingrained in his nightly routine, contributing to better sleep hygiene practices.
While headaches persist, they now occur approximately twice weekly, with a moderate intensity. Mr. Smith states that ibuprofen 400 mg remains effective for symptomatic relief when needed, and he has been assessing the impact of amitriptyline, which he has adjusted to 20 mg nightly upon the previous recommendation. He reports a subjective decrease in headache frequency, attributing this to the combination of amitriptyline and improved stress management techniques.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Melatonin 5 mg at bedtime 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 4. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief 5. Amitriptyline 20 mg nightly
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, reporting that he has been proactive in managing work-related stress through effective time management and prioritization of tasks. He remains committed to his walking routine and has increased mindfulness meditation sessions to daily practice, which he finds beneficial for both mental and physical health. He maintains abstinence from alcohol and has begun exploring a plant-based diet, which he feels has positively influenced his energy levels.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Notable decrease in anxiety frequency; improved sleep quality; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Reduced tension-type headache frequency; no visual changes or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue noted, though improved; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert and oriented, in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears moderately anxious, with noted improvement.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Consider discussing the use of lorazepam for acute anxiety episodes as needed, while continuing to reinforce non-pharmacological strategies. 2. Insomnia: Maintain melatonin at 5 mg at bedtime; continue to emphasize CBT-I strategies. Monitor sleep patterns and consider a sleep study if no further improvement is noted. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue ibuprofen as needed; assess efficacy of amitriptyline at 20 mg nightly and consider further adjustments if headache frequency does not improve. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue encouraging physical activity and mindfulness practices; revisit dietary optimization with nutritionist referral if fatigue persists.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2027-08-01 to evaluate ongoing symptoms, assess treatment effectiveness, and discuss further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any worsening of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
